basis: Lysosomal storage disorder; intellectual disability in 80-99% and ataxia in 30-79%. Hearing, skeletal, ocular and immunodeficiency findings are below 30%.
Defined by congenital limb malformations; structural cardiovascular abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Ear abnormalities and hearing impairment occur in fewer than 30%.
Fungal infection; skin/nail infection and sinusitis/pneumonia each occur in 30-79%. Cytopenias usually predispose to infection; ocular disease is uncommon in supplied HPO data.
Acute malignant myeloid disease of blood and bone marrow; monosomy 7 does not establish another organ involvement.
Unilateral loss of labyrinthine vestibular function; parent explicitly identifies an inner ear disorder.
DSC2-related arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. Definition specifies isolated disease; keratoderma and woolly hair are not established as common across this subtype.
Cerebellar malformation and postaxial polydactyly define the syndrome, each reported in 80-99%. Frequencies of cardiac and damaging ocular abnormalities are unspecified.
Coloboma, cleft lip/palate and intellectual disability define the syndrome; hearing loss affects 10/11. Hematuria in 4/7 alone does not establish renal damage.
Substance dependence is a psychiatric disorder; substance-specific organ damage is not intrinsic to this umbrella concept.
Thymic epithelial tumor; thymus has no listed anatomical axis. It is not lymphoma or a blood-cell neoplasm; associated autoimmune diseases are separate.
Abnormal urinary protein excretion; explicitly classified as a kidney disorder.
Named defining abnormalities involve hair loss and congenital brain enlargement. No definition or phenotype evidence supports additional organs.
Most childhood carcinoids arise in the appendix or other gastrointestinal sites. Bronchial tumors are a minority; neuroendocrine differentiation alone adds no endocrine axis.
Cancer susceptibility without intrinsic organ damage; principal breast and ovarian sites lack axes. Pancreatic and other cancers are future risks, not existing involvement.
Viral infection located in the central nervous system; other organ involvement is not shared across this umbrella.
Tumor originates in the anal canal. Liver enlargement/enzymes do not establish common hepatic invasion; pulmonary carcinoid is a separate tumor, not anal tumor involvement.
Personality disorder without defining direct damage to any listed organ axis.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and seizures define the syndrome. Hypothyroidism affects 3/4 reported patients; cardiac defect occurs in only 1/5.
Schwann-cell tumor arising along the trigeminal cranial nerve.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease affecting the colon; extraintestinal damage is not established as common.
Extragonadal germ-cell tumor originates in the mediastinum, outside the listed anatomical axes. Lung, pleural or cardiac invasion is not established as common.
Atrial septal defect is a defining structural heart abnormality. Congenital lymphedema alone does not establish skin damage; other findings lack adequate frequency evidence.
Dissection directly damages the internal carotid artery. Ischemic stroke is a separately diagnosed complication, not inherent neurologic involvement.
Soft-tissue sarcoma usually arising in deep connective tissues of the extremities; biphasic describes histology, not another organ origin.
Reduced red-cell mass or hemoglobin defines a blood disorder. Dyspnea, palpitations and fatigue do not establish direct damage to other organs.
